name: vwap_mean_reversion_v19
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, moderate 20-35 spot point deviations from VWAP occur 5-10 times per session during normal trading. These are caused by short-term order flow imbalances — a cluster of sell market orders hitting the book within a 2-3 minute window, often from a single algo executing a parent order. Unlike the deep deviations (40+ points) that require sustained selling pressure, these moderate deviations resolve FAST because they don't reflect a change in sentiment, just a temporary supply surge. Market makers who are short gamma from option selling are the first to fade these moves — they need to delta-hedge by buying the dip, and they do so within 30-60 seconds of the deviation peak. At 5-second bars, we see the moment the market-maker buying begins: price forms a 2-3 bar base (10-15 seconds of no further selling) and then ticks up. We enter on the first uptick after the base and ride the quick 10-15 spot point bounce as market makers and VWAP algos pull price back toward the session average.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume) from session open
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP as fair-value anchor. Same as v18.

indicators.name: vwap_dev
indicators.purpose: Percentage deviation from VWAP. Using a LOWER threshold than v18 (-0.08% vs -0.15%) to catch moderate deviations that occur more frequently. On NIFTY, 0.08% = ~20 spot points, which is the minimum deviation where market-maker delta hedging becomes visible.

indicators.name: bar_range_6
indicators.purpose: 30-second price range to detect 'basing' behavior. Replaces the original's relative volume filter. When the 30-second range contracts to below 5 spot points after a 20+ point deviation, it signals the selling has stopped and a base is forming. This is the entry setup — the base before the bounce.

indicators.name: close_vs_low_6
indicators.purpose: Where current close sits within the 30-second range (0 = at low, 1 = at high). When this exceeds 0.7 during a VWAP deviation, price is bouncing off the recent lows — the first sign that market-maker buying is absorbing the sell flow. Original had no equivalent; this is new for 5s resolution to time the exact bounce start.

conditions: vwap_dev < -0.08 (NIFTY is 20+ spot points below VWAP)
bar_range_6 < 8 (30-second range has contracted — selling has paused, base forming)
close_vs_low_6 > 0.7 (price is bouncing off the base — market maker buying visible)
buy_ce.confirmation: Current bar close > previous bar close (uptick confirms bounce)

conditions: vwap_dev > 0.08 (NIFTY is 20+ spot points above VWAP)
buy_pe.confirmation: Current bar close < previous bar close

exit.stop_rationale: Tighter than v18's 6-point stop because these are SHALLOW deviations — if price moves another 8 spot points against us (4 option points), the deviation is deepening into v18 territory and our quick-bounce thesis is wrong. The moderate deviation has become a deep deviation, which is a different trade with different dynamics. Cut fast and potentially re-enter under v18's deeper threshold.
exit.target_rationale: Moderate VWAP deviations of 20-35 spot points typically revert 50-70% within 2-3 minutes. That's 10-24 spot points of bounce = 5-12 option points. Target of 6 captures the median expected bounce, giving 1:1.5 risk-reward. Lower target than v18 because the reversion magnitude is smaller — we compensate with higher trade frequency (4-8/day vs 1-3/day).

filters.vix_filter: none — moderate VWAP deviations happen in all volatility regimes
filters.time_filter: No trades before 09:25 (VWAP needs 10 min to stabilize) or after 15:15 (too close to EOD, VWAP algos winding down)
filters.volume_filter: replaced by bar_range_6 indicator (range contraction is a better signal than volume on index)
filters.trend_filter: none — counter-trend by design, but shallower deviations mean less trend-fighting risk
filters.spread_filter: skip if ATM option bid-ask > 2 points

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — market-maker delta hedging is structural, not behavioral

adaptation_notes: Original v19 was nearly identical to v18 but on 1-min bars with a tighter z-score (2.1 vs 1.7). Blindly converting both to the same 5s format would produce duplicates. Instead, differentiated by DEPTH OF DEVIATION: v18 targets deep deviations (0.15%+, 40+ spot points) with patient holds, while this v19 targets moderate deviations (0.08%+, 20+ spot points) with quick scalps. v19 uses a DIFFERENT ENTRY MECHANISM: instead of dev_momentum (rate of deviation change), it uses bar_range contraction + close position within range to detect micro-level basing behavior — something only visible at 5s resolution. This gives v19 a distinct microstructure edge from v18 even though both are VWAP reversion. Original's 20-bar stddev and relative volume were dropped: stddev replaced by fixed percentage threshold (more stable for an index), relative volume replaced by range-based indicators that capture the specific microstructure signal (base formation before bounce).
weaknesses: Higher false positive rate than v18 due to lower deviation threshold — some 0.08% deviations are noise, not signal
Quick bounce thesis fails on sustained selling days where every bounce is sold into
More trades per day means higher transaction costs — need >57% win rate just to break even after costs
Bar-range contraction can be caused by a brief pause before a LARGER selloff, not a genuine base
